From her handbag, Jessica extracts a newspaper clipping and unfolds it. "I don't know whether you've been following this case," she continues, "but here's a sample of what I'm up against." She reads:
 
"'Police have intensified their investigation into the brutal hit-and-run of real estate tycoon Walter Kincaid, who remains hospitalized since late Friday night. Although no witnesses to the incident have come forward, several people reported seeing a late-model white Jaguar convertible speeding through the area minutes before Kincaid was discovered. By all accounts, the driver, a blonde woman in her mid-twenties, was driving in a reckless and erratic manner. Authorities have not yet located the automobile; however, a similar vehicle is believed to belong to the victim's wife, who was not at home when the incident occurred.'" 
 
She glances up. "In case you haven't guessed, my car is a brand new '48 white Jag convertible. Or, rather, it was. It's missing." She wads the article into a ball and stuffs it back into her purse. "I'm in trouble, shamus. Deep trouble. I need you to get me out of it."
